scope.purpose: Bounded final visual QA of historically sensitive routing, authority, evidence, model-comparison, and recovery-objective views.

methodology.desktop: Opened the exact production preview at 1280 x 960, advanced by the rendered state counter, selected the named relationships, and captured the complete figure element at original resolution.
methodology.comparison: Inspected the security-model small multiples in the Clark-Wilson base states and the Bell-LaPadula/Biba and Brewer-Nash changed states. This renderer exposes each relationship directly rather than through a selector.
methodology.quantitative: Compared the base and changed RPO/RTO/MTD timelines against their numeric tables and captions on the shared time scale.
methodology.mobile: At 390 x 844, selected the D4 evidence relationship, scrolled the figure canvas from 0 to its maximum horizontal position, expanded the text equivalent, and verified that the page itself did not gain horizontal overflow.
methodology.sourceMutation: None by the reviewer. The finding was reported before the original D1-D4 author made the agreed one-file repair.
methodology.unchangedModelCarryover: The four unchanged target files retain the exact hashes reviewed on release 4b4af10e8b27cbea. Their semantic and full-size visual results carry forward to release 0605853d09809a70 because only d4-o01-network-segmentation-trust-zones changed; the new build uses the same reviewed renderer behavior. The changed D4 model was re-exercised separately at desktop and 390 px.

relationshipSelections.text: Deployment authority -> can change code, secret, route, and runtime configuration for -> Serverless intake function
Deployment authority -> can change approved image and orchestration policy for -> Containerized classifier

caseResults.observations: The source authority and the two distinct controlled runtimes remain visible across their lanes. The selected arrows terminate at the named workload and do not imply that the provider service path owns deployment authority. Labels, highlighted endpoints, caption, and text consequence agree.

Management authority points separately to north-south and east-west control surfaces. The two operational paths point separately to the network-evidence entity with labels specific to boundary decisions versus east-west identity and flow. Direction, endpoints, lane membership, and selector prose agree.

The bypass arrow correctly depicts an actually reached stale-rule path from the backup appliance to production. The original evidence view exposed SUP-D4-001; the separate final remediation case records its accepted replacement.

Clark-Wilson separates certified entry, independent approval, release, and IVP/audit evidence. Bell-LaPadula shows no-read-up, strict Biba shows no-read-down, and Brewer-Nash keys denial to prior conflict history. Highlighted cards change with the exact state; inactive comparisons remain visible for context without being styled as the focal relation.

On the shared scale, the base snapshot at -1 hour is outside the -0.25-hour RPO while acceptance at +3.5 hours is within the +4-hour RTO and +6-hour MTD. In the changed state, the current recovery point meets RPO, but acceptance at +7 hours exceeds both RTO and MTD. The drawn segments, labels, table values, and captions agree.

The figure can be scrolled to the rightmost management lane without creating body-level horizontal overflow. The expanded text equivalent lists all six entities and seven relationships and remains readable. It faithfully repeats the selected evidence relation, so SUP-D4-001 applies equally to the visual and text forms.

desktopSelections.text: Research crossing PEP -> contributes its local research-crossing record to -> Evidence comparison
Brokered administrator path -> contributes its separate local administrator-session record to -> Evidence comparison

caseResults.observations: Both selectors now terminate at the neutral Evidence comparison entity. The research PEP and administrator broker remain distinct sources with distinct local-record labels; neither is drawn as the destination of the other. The desktop canvas exposes each full selected source and target with local scrolling. At 390 px, both locally scrolled views preserve body width, and the expanded text equivalent names both distinct contributions and states that neither policy point is the source or destination of the other record.

findings.actual: The boundary renderer draws a directional arrow from Research crossing PEP to Brokered administrator path for the label 'records research-flow evidence distinct from the administrator-path evidence at'.
findings.impact: The arrow geometry can be read as research evidence flowing into the administrator path, although the state statuses describe two separate local records: research permit/deny evidence at the PEP and authenticated administrator-session evidence at the management broker.
findings.expected: Show the two policy points recording their own evidence, compared through a neutral evidence/accounting entity or other noncausal comparison geometry. Do not imply that one policy point sends its record to the other.
findings.agreement: Root agreed this requires repair and assigned the original D1-D4 author to change only this model. The reviewer made no source edit.

remediation.implementation: Added neutral Evidence comparison node. Research crossing PEP contributes its local research-crossing record to it; Brokered administrator path contributes its separate local administrator-session record to it. The evidence state activates both sources, the neutral comparison, and both evidence edges, and explicitly says the records remain distinct.
remediation.validation: Exact hashes recomputed; effective endpoints and active references inspected; content validator passed. On the immutable regenerated candidate, both edges were selected and inspected at 1280 px and 390 px; both mobile text equivalents were expanded; no body-level horizontal overflow occurred.

summary.nextStep: None. The bounded supplemental visual review is complete and SUP-D4-001 is closed on the final immutable release.
